summary: Tested Wayly BOS iteration — 5A.1 Marketing Investment Intelligence, 5A.2 Founder Command Centre, 4A Growth Engine, 4B Growth Pipeline. Backend pytest suite: 27/28 passed, 1 skipped (depends on failed test), 1 real failure caused by Decimal128 serialization bug in GET /api/admin/marketing/campaigns/{id}. All 4 admin pages (/admin/command-centre, /admin/growth-engine, /admin/growth-pipeline, /admin/marketing-spend) render with their declared root data-testids. Command Centre inner data-testids (cc-needs-attention/cc-trends/cc-approval-centre/cc-alerts/cc-briefing/cc-integration-health) are all present. ZZTEST synthetic data hard-cleaned after the run.

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 with TypeError: 'Decimal128' object is not iterable when the campaign has an approved_budget_aud (stored as Decimal128 by POST /campaigns/{id}/budget). The response dict `{campaign: c, expenses, ...totals}` is passed to FastAPI jsonable_encoder with the raw Mongo Decimal128 still inside the campaign doc. This also breaks the /admin/marketing-spend page which shows 'Could not load setup data' banner whenever a campaign has an approved budget. Fix: run the campaign through a _campaign_public() serializer (same as _expense_public) that converts Decimal128 → float via to_aud(D(...)).

ui_bugs.issue: Toast 'Could not load setup data' appears on page load after a budget is set — caused by the backend 500 above (campaign GET). Fixing the backend serialization resolves this.

Observed data-testid is 'spend-add-expense'; task spec referenced 'exp-committed/exp-incurred/exp-paid/exp-publisher' modal field testIDs. Modal was not opened during this run, so presence of those field testIDs inside the modal was not UI-verified (backend accepts the new fields — covered by pytest). Recommend main agent self-verify the modal field testIDs match the spec.

rca of the issue: GET /api/admin/marketing/campaigns/{id} builds its response as `{"campaign": c, "expenses": [...], **totals}` where `c` is the raw Mongo doc (minus _id). After POST /campaigns/{id}/budget stores approved_budget_aud via to_decimal128(), the campaign doc holds a bson.Decimal128 value. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot iterate/serialize Decimal128, raising `TypeError: 'Decimal128' object is not iterable` (and the fallback `vars()` error). Fix: introduce a `_campaign_public(c)` similar to `_expense_public(e)` that walks known Decimal128 fields (approved_budget_aud today; any future ones) through `to_aud(D(...))`. Optionally register a fastapi/pydantic JSON encoder for Decimal128 globally.
